name: Rijksakademie van beeldende kunsten (Cavaleriekazerne)
description: A neoclassical cavalry barracks of 85 by 56 metres, built in 1864 to a design by the Dutch Ministry of War, with quarters for the troopers and stables for the horses; a riding hall was added ten years later. The army left in 1988, and after a large conversion the Rijksakademie van beeldende kunsten, the national academy of fine art, moved in from the Stadhouderskade. The old ranges now hold artists' studios, and in 1991-1992 Koen van Velsen added a new exhibition and library building in the courtyard and a steel-and-glass canteen on the water, linked by skybridges.
funFact: The plaque over the gate still reads KAVALLERIE-KAZERNE, in the old spelling of cavalry; the barracks played a part in the Dutch Water Line and the Defence Line of Amsterdam.
